data.title: Sandisk Stock Just Split 8-for-1 — Why It Matters for Investors
data.description:
Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) is entering a new chapter on Wall Street today, with its shares beginning to trade at a split-adjusted price following an 8-for-1 stock split. The move means investors now own eight shares for every one they previously held, while the price of each share has been divided by eight. Based on Thursday's closing price of $755.16, that translates into a new starting price of about $94.40 per share.

The split comes at a particularly challenging time for Sandisk, with shares having lost about 48% of their value over the past month.

Why Sandisk's Stock Split Matters for Investors

For existing shareholders, the immediate impact is purely mathematical. Someone who owned 10 Sandisk shares before the split now holds 80, but the total value of that investment remains unchanged. The company's market cap, earnings, and underlying financial position are also unaffected.

However, the lower share price could have some practical advantages. At more than $750 per share, buying Sandisk required a relatively large investment for anyone whose brokerage doesn't support fractional shares. With the stock now trading around $94 on a split-adjusted basis, smaller investors can purchase whole shares more easily. That could broaden the potential buyer base and potentially encourage additional trading activity.

There's also a psychological element worth considering. Stocks trading at lower nominal prices can appear more affordable, even when their valuations haven't changed. While that doesn't guarantee stronger demand, greater accessibility could help Sandisk attract retail investors who previously considered its shares too expensive.

Ultimately, the split doesn't make Sandisk cheaper based on earnings or future cash flows. Nor does it protect shareholders from further losses. For investors considering buying the stock, the real opportunity depends on whether Sandisk can maintain its profitability and whether the recent sell-off has gone too far.

Why Has Sandisk Stock Been Falling?

At first glance, Sandisk's financial results hardly seem to justify such a steep sell-off. On October 29, the company reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.03 billion, up 378% year-over-year and above Wall Street's $10.72 billion estimate. Adjusted earnings reached $49.51 per share, beating expectations of $46.67. Looking ahead, Sandisk also offered an encouraging outlook, projecting second-quarter earnings of $55 to $57 per share on revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion, both ahead of analysts' forecasts.

However, investors appear worried about what comes next for the NAND flash memory market. One turning point came when Japanese memory manufacturer Kioxia warned that the rapid increase in NAND prices was slowing. Its average selling prices rose in the mid-20% range during the September quarter, compared with a 70% increase in the preceding period. That raised concerns that Sandisk's unusually high profitability could become harder to maintain.

Those worries have continued growing throughout November. Investors are concerned that weaker demand for consumer electronics, combined with increasing memory supply, could eventually push NAND prices lower. Sandisk has also suffered from the broader sell-off in AI-related stocks, as Wall Street reassesses whether spending on data centers and computing infrastructure can continue at its current pace.

The latest warning came from research firm TrendForce, which expects NAND contract prices to begin falling in the first quarter of 2027. The firm also reduced its forecast for fourth-quarter 2026 price increases to between 8% and 13%, giving investors another reason to remain cautious.

Despite these concerns, Sandisk continues working to secure long-term agreements with data center customers, potentially providing greater revenue visibility if memory prices weaken.

What Does Wall Street Expect Next?

Despite Sandisk's steep losses, Wall Street remains bullish on the stock. SNDK currently holds a Strong Buy consensus rating, based on 11 Buys and 3 Holds issued over the past three months. The average 12-month price target stands at $2,003.23, implying upside potential of 165% from the pre-split price of $755.16. (See SNDK stock forecast)
data.author: Ben Yoffe

data.title: U.S. Stock Futures Under Pressure as Anthropic Falls After Stellar Debut
data.description:
U.S. stock futures fell Friday morning as Anthropic's (ANT) shares declined following the artificial intelligence (AI) company's blockbuster market debut yesterday. The decline in ANT and AI trade concerns weighed on investor sentiment on technology stocks. Futures on the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) fell 1.89%, 0.89%, and 0.43%, respectively, as of 8:35 a.m. EST on November 20.

Oil prices declined on Friday morning as investors digested reports of global supply surplus. However, geopolitical risks persist amid Houthi attacks in Riyadh and reported disruptions to oil tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, fell 0.45% to $91.57 per barrel, while WTI crude futures declined 1.03% to $82.35 per barrel.

During Thursday's regular trading session, major U.S. stock indexes fell more than 2% each. The sell-off came despite an initially positive session, when the Nasdaq Composite gained as much as 2.1% and the S&P 500 rose 1.3%. However, stocks reversed course shortly after Anthropic began trading. Notably, the Dow Jones closed below the crucial 50,000 level for the first time since June.

In pre-market trading, Intuit (INTU) stock fell after the tax software company announced a $3.68 billion sale of Mailchimp to Bending Spoons (BSP). The company also lowered its full-year revenue outlook due to weakness in the Credit Karma business. Shares of off-price retailer Ross Stores (ROST) trended lower after its fiscal fourth-quarter outlook failed to impress investors.

In contrast, Gap (GAP) stock rose after the apparel company's Q3 earnings beat expectations. Meanwhile, UnitedHealth (UNH) stock rose in premarket trading after TD Cowen upgraded its rating on the health insurer to Buy from Hold.

data.title: SpaceX Sold $32B of Bonds at 8%+ Yields to Buy AI Chips; SPCX Stock Falls
data.description:
Aerospace company SpaceX (SPCX) sold $32 billion of bonds on Thursday to fund its purchase of AI chips. According to Bloomberg, the transaction was complex and involved high yields. Investors had already committed to buy about $26 billion of the bonds earlier. The final $6 billion, which was part of the Class A3 notes, was offered yesterday. SPCX stock fell in Friday's pre-market trading.

Shares have been under pressure amid a broader tech and AI pullback. Investors have been concerned about steep valuations, returns on massive investments, and the sustainability of high AI spending.

SpaceX is raising more than $40 billion through a broader transaction, including the bonds sold on Thursday and a senior secured loan. The proceeds will be used to pay for about $47.3 billion of graphics processing units (GPUs), mainly Nvidia's (NVDA) Rubin chips.

More on SpaceX's Debt Offering

Citing sources, Bloomberg reported that SpaceX's debt offering was sold in three parts, with Goldman Sachs (GS) and Apollo (APO) managing the transaction. Notably, the largest portion, involving about $25.2 billion of Class A3 notes, was priced at an 8.259% yield, well above the 5.95% average yield on U.S. investment-grade bonds.

Moreover, the new bonds were priced above SpaceX's June debt offering, which had fallen in the secondary market after issuance. The transaction's structure is designed to help SpaceX maintain its investment-grade credit rating, which is crucial for raising larger amounts of money at a lower cost.

Furthermore, SpaceX is buying AI chips through Saturn Funding Trust, a special-purpose vehicle managed by an Apollo-backed entity. Rather than owning the equipment, SpaceX will lease GPUs from this vehicle. The company has agreed to keep making lease payments even if the equipment fails or an extraordinary event (such as a natural disaster) occurs.

Tech and AI companies have been raising massive amounts to fund data center and AI infrastructure investments. However, the latest financing structure was difficult for investment-grade investors to assess, as deals backed by AI GPUs are still relatively new, making it hard to evaluate how long the chips will remain useful and what they will be worth over time.

Is SPCX Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Given strong space and AI-related growth opportunities, Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on SpaceX stock based on 28 Buys, six Holds, and one Sell. The average SPCX stock price target of $263.83 indicates 90.6% upside potential.

data.title: ANT vs. NVDA – Why Cathie Wood Bought $91M in Anthropic and Sold Nvidia
data.description:
Cathie Wood's ARK Invest purchased 934,968 shares of Anthropic (ANT) worth about $91 million as the Claude maker made its Nasdaq (NDAQ) debut at a roughly $1.8 trillion valuation. According to the firm's November 19 trade disclosures, ARK also sold 33,430 shares of Nvidia (NVDA), worth approximately $4.88 million. Nvidia stock has faced recent pressure amid concerns over U.S. investigations into the possible sale of its chips to China against export rules.

Wood discussed ARK's Anthropic investment and its changing Nvidia exposure in an interview with ETF IQ Asia. She highlighted the firm's conviction in enterprise AI and its evolving approach to selecting technology investments.

ARK Invest Builds Its Anthropic Position

Wood is very optimistic about Anthropic's role in the enterprise AI market, pointing to the rapid growth of the AI industry. She believes the AI revolution is still in its early stages, leaving significant room for further growth.

She also sees healthcare as one of AI's biggest uses in the long run. She noted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's background in biotech and his focus on using AI in healthcare.

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, November 19, after pricing its IPO at $83 per share. The company raised approximately $81.3 billion, making it the largest initial public offering on record. Shares opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17, gaining 17.1% over the IPO price. However, the stock subsequently declined nearly 5% in overnight trading and remained under pressure in premarket trading.

The company's prospectus showed revenue of $33.24 billion for the nine months ended September 30, up 1,200% year-over-year. Revenue also grew 47% from the prior quarter.

ARK Trims Nvidia Exposure

Nvidia shares fell 3.3% on Thursday, extending their losing streak to six sessions. The stock has also come under pressure after reports that California is looking into whether Nvidia chips were sent to China against U.S. export rules. On November 16, ARK sold 543,092 shares worth about $84.8 million.

Despite the recent fall in its stock, Nvidia continues to report strong growth. The company posted quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year-over-year, while data center revenue rose 110% to $107.6 billion.

Wood said ARK first bought more Nvidia shares during the market dip as it focused on stocks it had the most faith in. However, following reports about Jensen Huang, ARK reassessed Nvidia through its internal investment scoring system, which looks at its people, leaders and work culture.

Wood said ARK downgraded Nvidia's score on these factors and moved some of its money from Nvidia into SpaceX (SPCX). She also sees strong growth ahead for SpaceX's AI business, led by its Grok model, which she thinks could compete with OpenAI and Anthropic at a lower cost.

Which AI Stock Do Analysts Prefer?

According to TipRanks Stock Comparison Tool, Anthropic has a Strong Buy consensus rating, while Nvidia carries a Moderate Buy rating. However, Nvidia offers a higher implied upside of 59.3%, compared with 37.2% for Anthropic.

data.title: SpaceX's New 'Game Plan' Could Pay Off, Says Top Analyst
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) has a "game plan" for its huge AI data center expansion, and Bernstein analyst Douglas Harned believes it could pay off. The company wants to build computing capacity quickly while demand is high and prices remain strong. This could help it recover its investment before computing prices fall. The facilities could also support Elon Musk's longer-term plans for AI data centers in space.

The 4-star analyst reiterated an Outperform rating and a $268 price target, implying 87% upside potential. Harned said the ground-based AI buildout "is not crazy," despite investor concerns about its cost and speed.

SpaceX Could Recover Its Investment in Less Than a Year

Bernstein believes the current shortage of AI computing capacity gives SpaceX a chance to earn back its investment quickly. Musk wants to add at least 20 gigawatts (GW) of power infrastructure and 10GW of computing capacity by the end of 2027. SpaceX expects to have about 3GW of computing capacity by the end of 2026.

Bernstein estimates the first 10GW could cost about $350 billion. Investors have questioned this spending because many neocloud providers charge less than $15 per watt for existing capacity.

However, SpaceX has already signed deals at around $30 and $50 per watt. Bernstein also noted that CoreWeave (CRWV), Nebius (NBIS), and IREN (IREN) reported higher prices for new contracts. These deals ranged from $20 to $45 per watt.

Harned believes SpaceX can approach $50 per watt in the first half of 2027. He wrote that if the company captures this price, "it can monetize the investment in less than 12 months."

Bernstein expects prices to fall as more data centers come online in 2028 and 2029. It sees raw computing prices declining to $13 to $15 per watt by 2030 and 2031. This makes speed crucial. SpaceX needs to secure high prices before more capacity enters the market.

Building Data Centers Quickly Will Be Crucial

The plan also depends on how fast SpaceX can bring new capacity online. Bernstein points to the company's work at its Colossus II data center complex in Memphis and South Haven.

SpaceX brought its first 210-megawatt cluster online in 91 days. The second cluster took just 64 days. Bernstein said the company achieved this by reusing existing industrial sites and building power systems alongside the data centers.

However, repeating this speed on a much larger scale will be harder. Bernstein expects SpaceX to add an average of 1.6GW of computing capacity each quarter over the next nine quarters.

The firm also flagged a possible shortage of high-pressure turbine blades. SpaceX wants to make its own blades, but Bernstein does not expect significant output before 2028. Any delay could make the expansion harder to complete before AI computing prices fall.

Ground Data Centers Could Support SpaceX's Plans in Space

Bernstein sees another use for the ground-based data centers once AI computing prices decline. SpaceX could use them to train its Grok models or sell capacity to other customers at market prices.

The facilities could also work alongside the company's planned orbital data centers. Some customers may prefer to keep their data on Earth rather than rely only on computing systems in space.

Bernstein expects orbital computing capacity to exceed ground-based capacity by 2031. Its model sees 27GW of orbital capacity and 20GW on the ground by then. SpaceX, however, has forecast a much larger 77GW orbital network.

Harned said the recent second-stage catch of Starship Flight 15 has increased his confidence in orbital AI. Still, he believes SpaceX does not need to reach its full orbital target to support the stock's valuation.

Is SPCX Stock a Good Buy?

Analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on SPCX stock based on 28 Buys, five Holds, and one Sell assigned in the past three months. The average SPCX price target of $267.76 per share implies 93% upside potential. (See SPCX stock forecast).

data.title: Alphabet Stock (GOOGL) Drops Nearly 20% to 2025 Bargain Levels as Top Trader Sees Two Signs of a Rebound
data.description:
Shares of Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) have dropped nearly 20% over the past month, returning the stock to its 2025 bargain levels. Despite the large pullback in GOOGL stock, veteran market chartist Larry Williams sees two signs that Alphabet shares may be ready to rebound, CNBC host Jim Cramer said on Mad Money on Thursday evening.

Google's Search Revenue Slowdown Sinks Alphabet Stock

Worries over Google's core business started after Alphabet published its third-quarter financial report on October 28. Alphabet shares plunged 12.6% the next day on October 29, marking the stock's worst one-day post-earnings drop on record. That single-day slide wiped out about $500 billion in market value.

Google Search and other ad revenue rose 12% in the third quarter to $63.4 billion, according to Alphabet's earnings release. That growth slowed from 17% in the second quarter and missed Wall Street forecasts near $65 billion.

On the October 28 earnings call, Alphabet Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler tied part of that slowdown to the company's new AI search tool. "It's worth noting that the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we're seeing in AI Mode," Schindler said.

In plain terms, each AI search brings in less ad money than a normal Google search. This fed worries that AI tools could eat into Google's main profit engine, Morningstar (MORN) noted.

Investors sold the stock even though Google Cloud revenue more than doubled from a year ago to $30.7 billion in the same quarter. Broader tech selling added pressure on November 16, when an AI stock rout wiped roughly $2.2 trillion from global markets, Deutsche Bank (DB) strategists noted.

Alphabet Shares Return to 2025 Valuation Lows

These back-to-back drops form the basis of Larry Williams' first rally signal. Alphabet stock now trades at roughly 15 times projected 2026 earnings, according to Williams' chart analysis shared on CNBC.

Over the past five years, Alphabet shares have usually traded between 20 and 30 times earnings. Today's price-to-earnings ratio puts the stock back near where it bottomed during an earlier search scare in spring 2025.

At that time, traders feared OpenAI's ChatGPT would pull everyday users away from Google Search. In April 2025, Alphabet traded near 16.9 times forward earnings, making it the cheapest stock in the Magnificent Seven tech group, TipRanks data shows.

Sentiment flipped later that year after quarterly results showed Google's AI features were lifting ad sales, Reuters reported. From that spring 2025 low, Alphabet shares more than doubled in just over a year.

Larry Williams Spots Big Investors Buying Shares

Williams uses a second chart signal to check whether big investors are stepping back into the stock. He pairs a value model that flags cheap shares with a buying gauge that tracks demand from large professional investors.

In past years, Alphabet shares formed major price bottoms and rallied largely whenever both tools flashed green at the same time. This exact pairing showed up earlier in 2026 right before a strong run in Alphabet stock.

Both signals have lined up again this week. Williams' model marks Alphabet as undervalued, while his buying gauge shows large investors have scooped up shares at a fast clip over the past four weeks. "This pattern, as Williams sees it, is bullish, and should result in higher prices," Cramer told viewers on Thursday.

Record AI Spending Drains Alphabet Cash Flow

Any rebound this winter faces a much larger spending bill than Alphabet carried in 2025. Back in February 2025, Alphabet set a $75 billion capital spending plan for that year in its fourth-quarter earnings report.

Alphabet now projects full-year 2026 capital spending of $195 billion to $205 billion, with most of the money going toward AI servers and data centers. Company executives also told analysts on October 28 to expect another big jump in spending in 2027.

Capital spending hit $51.4 billion in the third quarter alone, more than double the prior year's level, Alphabet's quarterly report showed. Moreover, large AI outlays and higher equipment costs pushed Alphabet's third-quarter free cash flow to negative $9.1 billion.

Doubts over big tech spending are weighing on the wider stock market as well. In Bank of America's November Global Fund Manager Survey released Tuesday, 34% of fund managers named an AI bubble as the top market risk. Another 31% pointed to debt trouble at big AI cloud spenders.

For Alphabet to repeat its 2025 comeback, Search ad growth may need to stablize first as its AI bills keep climbing.

Is Google Stock a Strong Buy Right Now?

Turning to the Street, Alphabet's stock (GOOGL) carries a Strong Buy consensus based on 30 Buy and four Hold ratings assigned in the past three months. The average 12-month GOOGL stock price target is $398.50, which implies 45.15% upside from the current price. (See GOOGL stock forecast)
